intro: Learn basic food words and meal times, along with their key verbs.
b1.titulo: The three meals of the day
b1.texto:
The three main meals are **el desayuno** (breakfast), **la comida** or **el almuerzo** (lunch), and **la cena** (dinner).
Each meal has an equivalent verb:
- **desayunar** → *Desayuno café con pan.* (I have coffee and bread for breakfast)
- **comer** → *Como arroz o verdura a las dos.* (I eat / have lunch at two)
- **cenar** → *Ceno huevos con patatas.* (I have eggs and potatoes for dinner)

Physical needs use the verb **tener**:
- **Tengo hambre** (I am hungry).
- **Tengo sed** (I am thirsty).

With gustar, foods take definite articles: *Me gustan **las** manzanas*.
b4.texto: Notice the use of meal verbs like cenar and idioms with tener like tener hambre.
b6.pregunta: Which meal is eaten in the morning?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! Breakfast is the morning meal.
b6.o1.refuerzo: La cena is dinner, eaten in the evening.
b6.o2.refuerzo: La comida is lunch, eaten at midday.
b7.pregunta: Choose the right article for general preferences.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Gustar takes the definite plural article las.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Manzanas is plural feminine, so it requires las.
b7.o2.refuerzo: General preferences use the definite article.
p.la naranja.consejo: Citrus fruit with lots of juice.
p.la patata.consejo: Standard in Spain; Latin America uses papa.
p.el zumo.consejo: Standard in Spain; Latin America uses jugo.
p.la comida.consejo: Midday meal or food in general.
p.comer.consejo: To eat food or have the midday meal.
b2.f0.texto: What do you have for breakfast in the morning?
b2.f1.texto: I have bread with tomato and cheese for breakfast.
b2.f2.texto: I have fruit and an orange juice.
b2.f3.texto: What time do you have lunch at midday?
b2.f4.texto: At two I eat rice or vegetables.
b2.f5.texto: Today I'm having eggs with potatoes for dinner.
b4.e0.texto: We have fish with white rice for dinner.
b5.f0.texto: Every morning we prepare breakfast with hot coffee and toast.
b5.f1.texto: My little brother eats a red apple and drinks a glass of milk.
b5.f2.texto: We all eat together at three in the dining room of our house.
b5.f3.texto: For the main meal we always cook rice with fresh vegetables.
b5.f4.texto: In the evening we have a light soup and an omelette with tasty potatoes.
b5.f5.texto: When we are thirsty we drink natural, freshly squeezed orange juice.
b8.frase: No me gusta la leche fría.
p.desayunas.consejo: The verb is made from the noun «el desayuno». The y sounds like the y in «yes».
p.tomo.consejo: Regular verb: «tomo», «tomas», «toma». The yo form ends in -o, like most verbs.
p.zumo.consejo: This is the word used in Spain; in Latin America they say «jugo». The z sounds like th.
p.naranja.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h: na-RAN-ha. The orange tree is «el naranjo».
p.verdura.consejo: It comes from «verde» (green). The v sounds like b: ber-DU-ra.
p.ceno.consejo: From «la cena» (dinner). The c before e sounds like th: THE-no.
p.pescado.consejo: A live fish is «el pez»; once caught to eat, it is «el pescado», from «pescar».
p.almuerzo.consejo: It goes with «almorzar»: the o becomes ue in «almuerzo». The z sounds like th.
p.preparamos.consejo: The «nosotros» form of «preparar»: all regular -ar verbs end in -amos.
p.manzana.consejo: The z sounds like th: man-THA-na. A red apple is «una manzana roja».
p.leche.consejo: The «ch» sounds like in «chocolate»: LE-che. «Café con leche» is a very common drink.
p.comedor.consejo: From «comer» + -dor: the place where you eat. Stress on the last syllable: ko-me-DOR.
p.cocinamos.consejo: From «la cocina» (kitchen). The c before i sounds like th: ko-thi-NA-mos.
p.sopa.consejo: A hot dish with broth: «sopa de verduras», «sopa de pollo». The stress falls on SO.
p.ligera.consejo: The g before e sounds like a strong h: li-HE-ra. The masculine is «ligero».
p.tortilla.consejo: In Spain «tortilla» (de patatas) is an egg omelette, not a flat bread. The ll sounds like y.
p.sed.consejo: You say «tener sed» (to be thirsty). It is a single syllable, said like «sed» in English.
p.bebemos.consejo: The «nosotros» form of «beber»: regular -er verbs end in -emos.
p.natural.consejo: «Zumo natural» is juice with nothing added. The stress is on the last syllable: na-tu-RAL.
p.exprimido.consejo: From «exprimir» (to squeeze). The x sounds like ks: eks-pri-MI-do.
p.rojas.consejo: Feminine plural of «rojo», agreeing with «manzanas». The j sounds like a strong h: RRO-has.
